bullets.title: META: Muse AI agent launch drives +5% move; Morgan Stanley calls it 'largest unpriced call option'
bullets.body: META's Muse personal AI agent launched with users consuming 10x more compute than test cohorts; pricing set at $0-$100/month. The underlying Watermelon model was trained with 10x more compute than prior generations, and Prometheus cluster already training post-Watermelon models. KeyBanc maintains Overweight citing low learning curve and distribution breadth; MS views stock at ~18x 2028 EPS with Muse as major upside optionality, though flags 2027 capex guide as near-term risk.

bullets.title: AAPL: Foldable iPhone Duo announced at $2,199 starting price, up from $1,999 target
bullets.body: Apple revealed the iPhone Duo foldable today with a $2,199 starting price and SKUs potentially reaching $3,000. Trade-offs vs conventional iPhone include weaker camera, shorter battery, and lower durability. No analyst action noted yet.

bullets.title: ALAB: Citi maintains Buy, $430 PT (+49%); Scorpio X ramp and optical optionality key catalysts
bullets.body: Revenue scaled from low tens of $M/quarter at IPO to $392M last quarter with EPS from ~$0.10 to $0.80. Scorpio X is in volume production and expected to become the largest product family by Q4, with content per XPU targeting well over $1,000. Citi models 80%+ EPS CAGR over 3 years and values ALAB at 40x P/E on estimated C28 EPS of ~$11; downside risks include share loss to AVGO/MRVL and customer concentration.

bullets.title: PINS: Down 5.6% at Goldman conf; EU regulation pressures international near-term despite AI ad momentum
bullets.body: Management highlighted H1 UCAN reacceleration and durable AI-driven ROAS improvements into Q3, with Performance+ handling ~30% of lower-funnel revenue. International business faces near-term headwind from new EU regulation limiting Asia cross-border sellers and internal go-to-market restructuring, creating medium-term pain before expected recovery. Gen Z is >50% of users with U.S. ARPU roughly in line with millennials.

bullets.title: CMCSA: CFO flags worsening broadband competition; Q3 subscriber losses unlikely to improve Y/Y, shares -5.3%
bullets.body: Comcast's CFO commented at the Goldman Sachs Communacopia conference that broadband competition is intensifying and Q3 subscriber losses are unlikely to improve year-over-year. CMCSA shares dropped 5.3% intraday on the comments.

bullets.title: GLW: Citi Buy, $220 PT (+32.6%); Verizon 80M+ fiber-mile deal accelerates $20B run-rate to Q3
bullets.body: Verizon awarded Corning a multi-year deal for 80M+ fiber miles (2027-2032) for broadband and data-center interconnect. Combined with Lumen and Zayo LTAs, management now expects to reach the $20B revenue run-rate one quarter earlier in Q3, with high-teens Y/Y growth continuing through Q4 and into 2027. Citi values GLW at 32x P/E on CY28 EPS; Springboard targets of $30B/$40B by 2028/2030 unchanged.

bullets.title: CRM: Citi Neutral, PT $233; Agentforce ROI still unproven but Claudeforce and public sector ARR >$2B driving optimism
bullets.body: Salesforce management noted AI is not yet visible on most customers' P&Ls, particularly in regulated industries, though Claudeforce adds 35+ prebuilt skills and Agentforce Operations (Regrello) is showing real PnL impact. Public sector ARR now above $2B with IL5/DoD authorization; MAX SKU and consumption-based pricing expected at Dreamforce next week. Citi PT $233 based on 11x forward EV/FY28 FCFF with 40% discount for competition and AI disruption risk.

bullets.title: FOXA/ROKU: DOJ Second Request received in merger review; deal still expected to close H1 2027
bullets.body: Fox Corp. and Roku each received a DOJ Second Request on Sept 8, extending the HSR waiting period. The deal, valued at $160/share ($22B enterprise value) with $400M run-rate cost synergies, remains on track for H1 2027 close pending stockholder approvals. Fox has $12B committed bridge financing from Morgan Stanley.

bullets.title: STX/WDC: HDD demand exceeds supply through FY27+; HAMR ramps and pricing power driving margin expansion
bullets.body: Seagate targets 25%+ exabyte CAGR with HAMR drives scaling from 30TB to 40TB and qualifying 50TB in ~1 year; opex flat at ~$300M/quarter. Western Digital sees cloud driving ~90% of HDD business with demand running above the 25%+ long-run CAGR view; 44TB HAMR targeted for H1 2027, 50TB+ to follow. Both companies see strong FCF generation with capital allocation shifting toward buybacks post-debt reduction.

bullets.title: NBIS: Full-stack hyperscaler buildout targeting 1GW this year, 5GW total; margin compression expected in 18-24 months
bullets.body: Nebius is transitioning from bare-metal GPU lessor to full-stack AI cloud, targeting mid-sized AI customers with 1-3 year commitments. Management sees current favorable supply-demand imbalance normalizing within 18-24 months, necessitating a fuller product stack; Palantir partnership is positioned as an enterprise channel step. Expansion constrained by capital needs, permitting, and construction delays.

bullets.title: MDB: Atlas traffic surging post-MCP rollout; investor day Sep 29; growth curve expected to bend as agents scale
bullets.body: MongoDB's managed MCP for Claude, Codex, and Grok launched Aug 13 and is driving materially higher Atlas traffic within 3.5 weeks. Growth acceleration is tied to customer-facing AI agents reaching production scale rather than internal use cases; banks, insurance, and healthcare still early. FedRAMP High investment targeting federal market; investor day set for Sept 29.

bullets.title: NYT: Citi Buy, $85 PT (+25%); confident on 15M subs by end-2027; video and AI licensing as growth drivers
bullets.body: Management is comfortable with the 15M subscriber target by year-end 2027, supported by a 150M+ registered user base. Video is now a major long-term priority with a three-phase rollout (production, engagement, monetization). Advertising is outperforming despite AI referral headwinds due to direct audience relationships and first-party data tools; Citi models 2027E EPS of $3.42.

bullets.title: VZ: Executing $9B cost plan; AI Connect $1B Google deal in pipeline; targeting 750k-1M net adds in H2
bullets.body: Verizon is cutting $5B in opex and $4B in capex while building an AI Connect revenue stream anchored by a $1B Google deal with more deals in pipeline. Mobility and broadband revenue grew 2.8% in Q2 with targets of 3% Q3 and 4% Q4; customers with both wireless and broadband see 30% lower churn. Fixed wireless access is growing and taking share.

bullets.title: ADBE: Q3 earnings preview; consensus $6.69B revenue/$6.08 EPS; options imply ~7.9% move
bullets.body: Street consensus for ADBE Q3 is revenue of $6.69B (vs guidance $6.67-6.72B) and EPS of $6.08 (vs guidance $6.05-6.10). The stock is up 17.6% since June 11 vs S&P +4.0%. Options imply ~7.9% move; last four quarter moves were -7%, -8%, +2%, 0%.

bullets.title: ORCL: F1Q27 preview; Street watching GPU capacity ramp, cloud growth acceleration, and OCI margin pressure
bullets.body: Consensus expects F1Q27 revenue of $19.135B with EPS of $1.74 and operating margin of 40.7%. Cloud revenue guidance calls for +58%-64% growth with acceleration expected in 2H27; investors focused on whether ~1GW of incremental capacity promised for F1Q was actually delivered. FY27 guidance includes gross margin pressure from OCI infrastructure ramp and $70B capex commitment.

bullets.title: BKNG: EU court upholds Etraveli acquisition block; stock down ~$10 on ruling
bullets.body: The EU General Court upheld the European Commission's 2023 decision blocking Booking's acquisition of Etraveli Group, rejecting Booking's appeal. The ruling reinforces Booking's dominant position concerns in EEA hotel OTAs. Booking continues its partnership with Etraveli through at least December 2028 as an alternative.

bullets.title: WULF/EQIX/DLR: Citi maintains Buy on data center REITs; constrained supply supports favorable leasing for 6-12 months
bullets.body: Citi raised price targets across the data center REIT space after Day 1 of its 2026 Global TMT Conference: DLR to $226, EQIX to $1,260, WULF to $31. Build costs have broadened to $10-20M per MW; firms with energized power pipelines can capture favorable leasing for at least 6-12 months. Post-midterm election removal of adverse regulatory attention expected to be a further catalyst.

bullets.title: SHOP: Wolfe Research call scheduled with Shweta Khajuria; stock +2.2% in pre-market
bullets.body: Wolfe Research analyst Shweta Khajuria is scheduled to speak with JAT's Don Liotine on SHOP. Shopify was trading +2.2% in pre-market amid retail sector strength.

bullets.title: ANET/CSCO: AI networking demand robust at GS conference; 5x bandwidth growth driving infrastructure buildout
bullets.body: Arista is seeing strong demand in AI networking particularly in back-end GPU interconnect networks, with scale-across deployments critical due to power and cooling constraints. Cisco noted agentic AI is driving a 5x increase in network bandwidth consumption across hyperscale, neocloud, and enterprise segments.

bullets.title: NOK: Morgan Stanley conviction buy on €2.8B Q2 order book; optical/IP growth potentially +22% in 2027
bullets.body: Nokia's Q2 order book hit €2.8B, 3x the Q1 level, with a second San Jose fab ramping late 2026/2027 and Pennsylvania capacity up 10x by end-Q3. Management's +6-8% mid-term revenue CAGR guidance is viewed as conservative vs. +12% H1 growth; optical/IP segment could grow +22% in 2027. Morgan Stanley rates NOK as a conviction buy dip.
